item.title: OpenAI Releases Codex Security for Vulnerability Detection and Remediation
item.description:
OpenAI Releases Codex Security for Vulnerability Detection and Remediation

OpenAI has released Codex Security, a toolset for finding, investigating, and fixing vulnerabilities in code. It provides security workflows accessible in Codex, a command-line interface, and a TypeScript SDK for automation.

🔍 Overview

Codex Security helps developers:

  • Scan repositories, selected paths, or Git changes
  • Validate candidate findings, generate patches, and verify existing fixes
  • Draft SECURITY.md policies and save threat models for later review
  • Browse saved scans and findings, identify duplicates, assess severity against custom rubrics, and suggest owners from source and Git history
  • Preview third-party scanner findings, save them locally, or publish supported reports to Codex Security Cloud

🧩 How It Works

Scan Types

  • Standard scans investigate code for vulnerabilities
  • Deep scans repeat Standard scans and return deduplicated findings
  • Scans use existing root and component SECURITY.md guidance
  • A completed scan saves a report and findings

Post-Scan Actions

  • Read the report for source evidence and exclusions
  • Request a patch or ask Codex to verify an existing fix
  • Track findings in Linear, Jira, or GitHub
  • Export results as SARIF, JSON, or CSV

⚙️ Key Details

Installation & Requirements

Component Requirement
Node.js 22.13.0+ within 22.x, or 24.x, or 26.x
Python 3.10+ (Python 3.10 also requires tomli)

CLI Usage

  • cs and codex-security run the same CLI
  • Use npx @openai/codex-security to skip global install or resolve EEXIST conflicts
  • Run cs scan . --max-time 15 for a 15-minute Standard investigation allowance
  • Use bulk scans for independent repository reviews in one resumable campaign
  • When the scan completes, open the Markdown file at the REPORT path in the terminal
  • Run cs scans show from the same repository to find its latest completed scan

CI Configuration

  • Set OPENAI_API_KEY or CODEX_API_KEY in the scan process’s environment

🔗 Integrations & Automation

  • Automate scans across repositories or project components, including in CI and containers
  • Publish completed scans to Codex Security Cloud (optional; local scans work without it)
  • When Codex Security Cloud is available, the Security plugin’s $cloud-findings skill reads findings, reports, recorded assignment and verification, and scan status in Codex desktop or the Codex CLI
  • Linked Git worktrees share scan history and saved findings when they use the same Codex Security state directory
  • Keep CODEX_SECURITY_STATE_DIR stable to retain shared history and sign-in scope

🔐 Advanced Features & Access Programs

  • Some cybersecurity requests and protected findings require Trusted Access for Cyber
  • For accounts with Daybreak access:
    • See Daybreak opt-in for the Codex toggle
    • See Cyber access programs to select a program explicitly
  • The SDK guide includes deep-scan configuration, validation, severity classification, owner suggestions, and result handling
  • Use policy to draft a new SECURITY.md or update an existing one
